heard: the undisputed largest star in the universe suddenly shrank in half. In 2012, astronomers measured the supergiant star, Ui Scuti, at 1,708 times the radius of our sun. Placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would swallow the orbit of Jupiter. That massive size estimate depended entirely on an assumed distance of 9,500 light years. But parallax data from the Gaia Space Telescope showed the star is actually 5,900 light-years away. In 2023, scientists recalculated its radius down to roughly 909 solar radii. While still a pulsating monster destined for supernova, its cosmic crown was gone. A simple distance measurement proved even the biggest legend can vanish overnight.
